audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 1 and 2 read 'Skill' in both layers while whys[0]/whys[1] state Sett wins both, and Levels 4-5 read 'Ryze' while whys[3] says neither kit overwhelms the other.
audit.why: Packet chart is Sett, Sett, Skill, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Ryze on a 49.85% / 339-game sample; the page's own prose agrees. Ryze has no W until 2 and no rotation until 3, and Pit Grit out-trades him level 1.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 -> Sett and row 3 -> Skill, proposed as matched full/content pairs with ratings.

audit.why: Sett spikes level 1-2 and at 6 with The Show Stopper; Ryze spikes at Rod of Ages and again at Seraph's. spikes[] and the first-item/two-item rows already carry this.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treated Facebreaker as an unconditional pull-stun ('stay off the line between him and units') and never stated the conditional. Riot's text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Its cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10) was never given either. Also, spikes[0] named the passive 'Hardest Hit' — Sett's passive is Pit Grit.
audit.why: Positioning on the same side as his minions downgrades the matchup-defining stun to a slow, which is the single most actionable fact in this lane and turns his engage into a Phase Rush trade window.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, whys[1] and spikes[0].text rewritten with the both-sides condition, the 16s rank-1 cooldown, and the real passive name.

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker's shield absorbing your burst window was flagged as a missing interaction and only half-covered by wants.you[0].
audit.why: Sett stores damage taken as Grit and cashes it as a shield plus true damage — bursting into a full Grit bar funds his own shield, so it has to be baited empty first.

edits.before: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides — stay on his minions' side and it is just a slow.

edits.before: Sett whiffs Facebreaker and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Haymaker turns your burst into his shield — bait it first.

edits.before: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Sett’s Facebreaker (16s at rank 1): it stuns only with enemies on both sides of him — stand on his minion side and you only take a slow.

edits.before: His Facebreaker grab is already available and your W root has a delay; if he grabs you mid-cast you lose the full combo — respect the stun and only W when he is committed forward.
edits.after: His Facebreaker is up already and runs 16 seconds at rank 1; it stuns only if enemies stand on both sides of him, so keep his minions and yourself on the same side and it downgrades to a slow.

edits.before: Sett's passive Hardest Hit double-punch and raw base stats let him win any straight trade before your W root is online — respect his auto-spacing.
edits.after: Sett's Pit Grit alternates punches — the right one hits harder and faster — and wins any straight trade before your W root exists; respect his auto-spacing.
